# Heterogeneous Dual-Brain SoC Reference Architecture {.unnumbered #sec-appendix-heterogeneous-soc}

This appendix defines the canonical reference architecture for heterogeneous dual-brain edge systems in Physical AI. It specifies the hardware topology, core partitioning, inter-processor communication (IPC) protocols, and hardware safety watchdog contracts that separate unprivileged stochastic policy deliberation from deterministic real-time safety enforcement.


## Dual-Brain System Topology

In an embodied machine, cognitive deliberation and mechanical actuation operate in fundamentally incompatible timing and determinism domains. The dual-brain architecture bridges this divide by mapping functional roles onto asymmetric processing domains on a shared System-on-Chip (SoC) or coupled compute module:

| Processor Subsystem | Architectural Core and OS | Primary Systems Role and Execution Contract |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Application Processor (MPU)** | Multi-core 64-bit Application CPU<br>Rich OS (Embedded Linux / RT-Linux) | **Untrusted Proposal Service:** Runs multimodal perception backbones, foundation models, ROS 2 stacks, and generative trajectory planners; emits timestamped, expiring candidate proposals ($p_t$). |
| **Real-Time Safety Controller (MCU)** | Deterministic Microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M / RISC-V)<br>Bare-Metal / Hard RTOS (Zephyr / FreeRTOS) | **Trusted Permission Authority:** Runs deterministic $1000\text{ Hz}$ control loops, Control Barrier Function safety filters ($h(x) \ge 0$), dynamic stopping enforcers ($d_{\text{stop}}$), and hardware PWM/timer registers. |
| **Inter-Processor Link (IPC)** | Shared SRAM Mailbox & Hardware Semaphore<br>RPMSG / OpenAMP Framework | Zero-copy lock-free circular ring buffers with atomic sequence counters, cache-coherent headers, and hardware mailbox interrupts. |


## Hardware Resource Partitioning

| Subsystem | Application Processor (MPU) | Real-Time Safety Controller (MCU) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Architecture** | Multi-core Out-of-Order Application CPU + NPU/GPU | Deterministic In-Order Microcontroller (Zero-Wait-State) |
| **Operating System** | Embedded Linux (Preempt-RT / Debian / Yocto) | Bare-Metal Firmware / Hard Real-Time OS |
| **Memory Subsystem** | 2 GB to 32 GB LPDDR4/LPDDR5 DRAM (Shared) | 256 KB to 1 MB On-Chip SRAM (TCM, Zero-Wait-State) |
| **Memory Management** | Virtual memory, TLB, demand paging | Physical addressing only, zero dynamic allocation (`malloc` prohibited) |
| **Execution Determinism** | Best-effort with tail jitter ($P_{99} \approx 20\text{--}80\text{ ms}$) | Hard real-time cycle predictability (WCET bounded, jitter $< 1\,\mu\text{s}$) |
| **Physical I/O Authority** | High-speed buses: MIPI CSI-2, USB 3.0, PCIe, GbE | Dedicated safety I/O: Timer PWM, Quadrature Encoders, Hardware E-Stop GPIO |


## Shared Memory RPMSG Message Contract

The application processor transmits timestamped intent proposals to the real-time safety controller over non-blocking shared SRAM mailboxes using the Remote Processor Messaging (RPMSG) protocol. The shared message schema (`PhysicalAgent_IntentProposal_t`) enforces a packed binary layout across cores:

| Field Name | Type | Size | Physical Units & Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `message_id` | `uint32_t` | 4 bytes | Monotonic proposal sequence counter. |
| `timestamp_us` | `uint64_t` | 8 bytes | 64-bit IEEE 1588 PTP synchronized hardware timestamp ($\mu\text{s}$). |
| `lease_duration_ms` | `uint32_t` | 4 bytes | Maximum validity lease duration before proposal expires ($\text{ms}$). |
| `target_pos_[x,y,z]` | `float[3]` | 12 bytes | 3D Cartesian spatial target coordinates in robot base frame ($\text{m}$). |
| `max_velocity_m_s` | `float` | 4 bytes | Maximum permissible Cartesian velocity envelope ($\text{m/s}$). |
| `max_acceleration_m_s2` | `float` | 4 bytes | Maximum permissible Cartesian acceleration bound ($\text{m/s}^2$). |
| `model_confidence` | `float` | 4 bytes | Epistemic model confidence score $\gamma_{\text{conf}} \in [0.0, 1.0]$. |
| `crc32` | `uint32_t` | 4 bytes | IEEE 802.3 32-bit CRC payload integrity checksum. |

: Physical AI Dual-Brain IPC Intent Proposal Schema. Binary layout of the packed shared-memory RPMSG payload. {#tbl-ipc-intent-contract}


## Hardware Safety Watchdog Protocol

The real-time controller monitors the application processor via a dedicated hardware countdown watchdog and heartbeat protocol:

1. **Heartbeat Packet:** The application processor must transmit an authenticated heartbeat packet every $\tau_{\text{ping}} \le 10\text{ ms}$.
2. **Watchdog Timeout:** If the real-time controller receives no valid heartbeat for $\tau_{\text{timeout}} = 50\text{ ms}$, an independent hardware timer triggers a Non-Maskable Interrupt (NMI).
3. **Hardware Action:** The real-time controller immediately de-asserts motor gate driver enable lines and transitions inverter power stages into a deterministic safe stop (Category 1 / Safe Torque Off) within $250\,\mu\text{s}$.
